	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/motionphoto"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/storage/s3"
	storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/server/auth"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
)

// Constants for file serving configuration.
const (
	// ThumbnailCacheFolder is the folder name where thumbnail images are stored.
	ThumbnailCacheFolder = ".thumbnail_cache"

	// MotionCacheFolder is the folder name where extracted motion clips are stored.
	MotionCacheFolder = ".motion_cache"

	// thumbnailMaxSize is the maximum dimension (width or height) for thumbnails.
	thumbnailMaxSize = 600

	// thumbnailMetadataProbeSize is the maximum number of original image bytes inspected
	// before thumbnail generation to detect metadata that the JPEG thumbnail pipeline cannot preserve.
	thumbnailMetadataProbeSize = 1 << 20

	// maxConcurrentThumbnails limits concurrent thumbnail generation to prevent memory exhaustion.
	maxConcurrentThumbnails = 3

	// cacheMaxAge is the max-age value for Cache-Control headers (1 hour).
	cacheMaxAge = "public, max-age=3600"
)

message.text: I will read the remaining parts of `serveUserAvatar` and `getUserByUsername` in `fileserver.go`, then trace `Store.GetUser` down to the driver layer.
Tracing the getUserByUsername and ListUsers chain to the database driver.

`user_service_converters.go` converts base64 avatars to `/file/users/{username}/avatar` paths.

The browser request hits `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes`, which registers the route to `serveUserAvatar`. That handler calls `Store.GetUser`, then `Store.ListUsers`, then the database driver. The avatar is stored as a data URI in the `user` table under `avatar_url`, and `serveUserAvatar` parses it back into a response.

`c.Blob` returns the image bytes. The browser learns the avatar URL from `convertUserFromStore` in `usverters.go`, which sets `AvatarUrl` to `/file/users/{name}/avatar` when the stored avatar is base64. The trace starts at `RegisterRoutes` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`.

`getUserByUsername` lives in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. `Store.GetUser` and `Store.ListUsers` are in `store/user.go`. The database driver is in `store/db/sqlite/user.go` or the equivalent for MySQL or Postgres. `server.go` wires the file server routes at startup.

The avatar URL path is `/file/users/{username}/avatar`, derived from `userpb.Name` being `users/{username}`.

Verifying the `ListUsers` function signature in `sqlite/user.go`.

The avatar is stored as a data URI in the `user.avatar_url` database column, not as a separate file.

The browser request `/file/users/{username}/avatar` is handled by `RegisterRoutes` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, then `serveUserAvatar` fetches the user via `Store.GetUser` and `Store.ListUsers` in `store/user.go`. The database layer is `(*DB).ListUsers` in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`, which executes a SQL `SELECT` for `avatar_url`. Finally, `parseDataURI` decodes the data URI from the `AvatarURL` string.

The decoded image bytes are written to the HTTP response by `c.Blob` in `server/router/fileserver/o`.

The trace stops at the data layer itself. `parseDataURI` and `c.Blob` are post-retrieval steps, not hops to stored data. The final hop is the driver-level `ListUsers` call in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`.

The browser loads another user's avatar at `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar` (URL built in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36` when the stored value is a base64 data URI). The request path to stored data:

RegisterRoutes — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (registers `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`; wired from `server/server.go:81-82`)

serveUserAvatar — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`

getUserByUsername — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-716`

Store.GetUser — `store/user.go:148-168`

Store.ListUsers — `store/user.go:136-145`

(*DB).ListUsers — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88-189` (equivalent in `store/db/mysql/user.go` and `store/db/postgres/user.go`)

SQL `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:151-189`

Stored data is the `avatar_url` column on the `user` table (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:20`), typically a base64 data URI. After fetch, `serveUserAvatar` decodes it via `parseDataURI` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196-209`) and returns the bytes with `c.Blob`.
